evidence_priority: recorded project decision or approved exception
repeated acceptable WIP corpus pattern in equivalent contexts
Ukrainian-language consultant or Area Linguist judgment
finding_requirement: A project-grammar finding must cite one or more rule IDs. A general meaning finding must identify its non-grammar category explicitly.
finding_requirements: Cite the exact WIP form and reference.
State the suspected Ukrainian relationship, not merely the REFERENCE difference.
Distinguish grammar, style, orthography, and meaning risk.
Route unconfirmed rules and naturalness judgments to the assigned human reviewer.

governance.authority: project-approved grammar guidance, corpus evidence, and recorded consultant decisions

restrictions: Do not infer a project rule from one occurrence.
Do not treat English REFERENCE grammar or word order as a model for Ukrainian form.
Do not transfer Greek or Hebrew morphology directly into Ukrainian grammar.
Do not auto-approve grammar decisions without project evidence or human review.
Do not turn an optional style preference into a meaning finding.

rules.caution: Apparent mismatch may be licensed by coordination, apposition, collective reference, or an implicit head.
rules.review: Check adjective, participle, pronoun, and predicate agreement for case, number, and gender where Ukrainian syntax requires it.

rules.caution: Do not force overt English-style subjects or resolve allowed singular/plural variation automatically.
rules.review: Check finite-verb agreement and the treatment of coordinated, quantified, impersonal, and understood subjects.

rules.caution: Lexical government and semantic role must be supported by Ukrainian evidence, not copied from REFERENCE order.
rules.review: Check case government by verbs, prepositions, adjectives, nouns, and fixed constructions.

rules.caution: Agreement can vary with syntax, animacy, and intended grouping; route disputed cases to human review.
rules.review: Check case/number patterns after cardinal numerals, collective numerals, quantities, and measure expressions.

rules.caution: Do not equate one Greek/Hebrew verbal form mechanically with one Ukrainian tense or aspect.
rules.review: Check whether aspect, tense, mood, voice, and reflexive forms preserve event structure and discourse function.

rules.caution: Avoid calques that are formally possible but unnatural or ambiguous in contemporary Ukrainian.
rules.review: Check control, attachment, temporal relation, and naturalness of infinitives, participles, and adverbial participles.

rules.caution: Preserve legitimate discourse prominence and avoid adding names solely to mirror REFERENCE repetition.
rules.review: Check pronoun antecedents, zero subjects, demonstratives, reflexives, possessives, and shifts between naming and pronominal reference.

rules.caution: Register and capitalization are project/community decisions, not automatic grammatical corrections.
rules.review: Check vocative forms, singular/plural address, capitalization, and ти/ви choices against project policy and discourse relationships.

rules.caution: A surface particle mismatch is not sufficient evidence of a meaning error.
rules.review: Check scope of negation, negative concord, particles, modal force, interrogatives, imperatives, prohibitions, and indirect commands.

rules.caution: Ukrainian word order is flexible; differences from English order are not findings by themselves.
rules.review: Check topic-focus order, contrast, emphasis, clitic/particle placement, and ambiguity created by constituent order.

rules.caution: Zero connectives and restructuring may be acceptable when the relationship remains clear.
rules.review: Check coordination, subordination, causal, inferential, adversative, concessive, temporal, and conditional relationships.

rules.caution: Confirm with Ukrainian corpus/project evidence before recommending change.
rules.review: Identify unnatural government, nominalization, passive, clause chaining, or modifier placement apparently copied from REFERENCE form.

rules.caution: Treat these primarily as style/orthography unless meaning, parsing, or readability is affected.
rules.review: Review у/в, і/й/та, з/із/зі and ся/сь choices where they materially affect fluency or project consistency.

rules.caution: Final naturalness and community acceptability require qualified Ukrainian speakers.
rules.review: Check contemporary Ukrainian idiom, genre, reverence/register, and accessibility for the project audience.

rules.caution: Do not apply English quotation conventions or move punctuation mechanically.
rules.review: Check Ukrainian quotation marks, nested quotations, dialogue paragraphing, and speaker changes against project policy.

rules.caution: Punctuation is partly stylistic; report only material or project-policy issues.
rules.review: Check commas, colons, semicolons, ellipses, em dashes, dialogue dashes, and spacing where they affect parsing or project consistency.

rules.caution: Do not normalize project-approved forms automatically.
rules.review: Check apostrophe forms, Ukrainian letter forms, capitalization, and orthographic consistency in the bounded text.

rules.caution: Do not revise a grammatically valid structure solely to match the contemporary reference; require a meaning, clarity, or project-policy reason.
rules.review: Check sentence division, clause attachment, parenthesis, coordination, and subordination where punctuation or word order permits competing parses.

usage.baseline_qa: Identify bounded evidence, corpus patterns, and review questions in the authorized scope.
usage.focused_check: Investigate one explicit grammatical concern using project and corpus evidence.
usage.initialization: Validate language identity, schema, and approval status; do not run verse-level grammar checks.
usage.original_language_review: Clarify source meaning only when materially relevant; do not prescribe Ukrainian form directly.
